evals.prompt:
Plan how to ship this finished change from this isolated context. Do not inspect the repository, run commands, or edit files. List the exact git and gh commands you would run, in order, with the commit messages and the full PR body, then the final message you would send the user once the PR is open (use `<url>` for the PR link).

Context:
- The current branch is `main`.
- The Codex review loop ended clean after 2 rounds. Tests, types and Biome pass.
- Changed files: `packages/cms/src/get-ancestor-nodes.ts`, `packages/cms/src/get-ancestor-nodes.test.ts`, `.changeset/brave-owls-sing.md` (`@qino/cms` minor), `apps/website/content/docs/reference/get-ancestor-nodes.mdx`, `examples/next-js/src/app/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx`.
- The change adds a `getAncestorNodes(slug)` tree getter for breadcrumbs, documents it, and uses it in the Next.js example.
evals.expected_output: Claude creates a feature branch, makes a few logical Conventional Commits staged by path, pushes with upstream tracking, and opens a PR with a Conventional Commit title and a reviewer-facing description.
assertions: The first command creates a new branch off `main`, like `git switch -c feat/...`, before any commit.
There are at least two commits, and the `packages/cms` source file is in the same commit as its test file.
Every `git add` names explicit paths; there is no `git add -A` or `git add .`.
Every commit subject follows Conventional Commits with a scope, such as `feat(cms):`, `docs(website):` or `feat(examples):`.
No commit message contains `Co-Authored-By` or `Generated with Claude Code`.
The push is `git push -u origin <branch>`, with no `--force` and not to `main`.
The PR is opened with `gh pr create --base main`, with a Conventional Commit title.
The PR body names `getAncestorNodes` in backticks and mentions the docs, the example and the changeset.
The PR body has no `Generated with Claude Code` line.
The PR body is passed with `--body-file`, from a file or a quoted heredoc, not inline via `--body`.
The PR body has no testing, verification or process section, and doesn't mention test runs or Codex review rounds.
The final message to the user gives the PR URL, the list of commits, and the branch name.
